clue.text: Put foot down to impress editor

parts.note: to stamp a mark is to impress it on a surface
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor laying down the law in order to make an impression on staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put foot down' sounds like being firm, but it is the literal act of bringing a foot down hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stamped brought a foot down heavily on the ground, the literal sense of the idiom.

clue.text: Get rid of earth from a graze

parts.note: to scrap something is to discard it
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Cleaning the dirt out of a grazed knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get rid of earth' reads as one instruction to clean a wound, but it splits into two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a minor skin wound caused by rubbing against a rough surface, the same injury as a graze.

clue.text: Dreads lousy summers?

indicators.note: something lousy is in poor shape, so the preceding word is badly arranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who hates a run of poor summer weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summers' is not the season but people who sum; the question mark flags the odd reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who do sums add numbers up, so summers in this playful sense are adders, a pun on the snake.

clue.text: Old slang being resurrected among locals in print

indicators.note: to be among things is to sit in their midst, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: a local is a pub, abbreviated PH for public house; two of them form the outside
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something resurrected rises up again, and in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: argot is the slang of a particular group

explanation.surface: Old slang words coming back into use among the people of a district and appearing in print.
explanation.walkthrough: PH is the map and directory abbreviation for public house, and a local is the pub nearest home, so the plural supplies a PH on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph developed onto paper is called a print, so the noun stands for the photographic image.

clue.text: King had this vision

parts.note: surface reading: a monarch saw something in a prophetic vision
setter's reading: Martin Luther King, whose famous speech declared that he had one

explanation.walkthrough: King is not a monarch but Martin Luther King, whose 1963 speech repeated the words 'I have a ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vision of a hoped-for future is an aspiration, and King's speech named his in exactly that word.

clue.text: He doesn't believe in organised life to accommodate daughter

indicators.note: to accommodate a guest is to take them inside, so one letter goes in among the rest
organised means put into a new order, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An atheist who rejects organised religion's view of life and takes his daughter with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a preposition after 'believe' but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is a person without religious faith, literally one who does not believe.

clue.text: Meddle in their offer regularly without hesitation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these letters wrap around another piece
regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone poking their nose into a deal being offered, and doing so without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'without' means outside here, so the alternate letters go round ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to involve yourself in matters that are not your concern, which is to meddle.

clue.text: Be unsuccessful in fighting against insurgency leaders, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Losing a campaign against the heads of a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like part of the insurgency picture, but it is the fourth word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail is to not succeed in an attempt, the plain sense of being unsuccessful.

clue.text: Give details of closure of watercress bed in river

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: the closure of something is its end, so the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a crib is a child's bed

explanation.surface: Someone shutting down a watercress bed in a river, since watercress grows in running water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watercress bed' reads as one thing, but the bed is separate wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to give an account of it, setting out its features in words.

clue.text: Teacher shows first sign of resentment after reprimand

parts.note: to lecture someone is to scold them at length

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A teacher shows a flicker of resentment after being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the single letter at the end of the reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer gives lectures at a university or college, so is a teacher at that level.

clue.text: Right fuss about start of interference on the wireless

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fuss goes round the next letter

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: Kicking up a fuss about interference on the wireless reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interference on the wireless' looks like a single phrase about static, but the definition is just the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless is the old-fashioned British name for a radio set, from transmission without wires.

clue.text: Foreign extremists reduced by 60% in western half of Sicily

indicators.note: cutting a ten-letter word by sixty per cent leaves only its opening four letters

parts.note: the first four of ten letters
taken as written

indicators.note: in an across clue the western half of a word is its left, opening half

parts.note: the first three of six letters

explanation.surface: Foreign extremists being cut down in the western part of Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in western half of Sicily' reads as a location, but 'in' supplies letters and 'western' means left-hand in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means coming from outside, so foreign to the thing in question.

clue.text: They put on an act, according to ex-head of state

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per instructions'
ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A former head of state accuses people of putting on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ex-head of state' looks like one title, but it splits into 'ex' and the first letter of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers such as actors and entertainers put on an act for an audience.

clue.text: Language of Monsieur Dupont

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the letters come from within the words after it

parts.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asking what language a Frenchman called Dupont speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The French name makes you think of French, but the language is tucked inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a language spoken in Pakistan and northern India.

clue.text: Still, try it on as a change!

indicators.note: a change of arrangement is called for, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Telling someone that standing still, or trying something on, might make a nice change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try it on' sounds like trying on clothes or chancing it, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means not moving, so it matches still used as an adjective.

clue.text: Proper to place berets askew

indicators.note: askew means crooked or out of line, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Is it correct to wear berets at a jaunty angle?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper to' reads as 'it is correct to'; the definition is only 'Proper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectable means socially acceptable and decent, a common sense of proper.

clue.text: Easily upset, it is even beginning to snow afresh

indicators.note: afresh means done over in a new way, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A worrier fretting that it is starting to snow again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like a selection signal for even letters, but here it is just part of the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive person is quickly hurt or offended, which is to say easily upset.

clue.text: In the end, she stops

indicators.note: In places the next piece inside the following phrase

parts.note: finis is Latin for the end, printed at the close of old books and films
taken as written

explanation.surface: A story's conclusion, where she comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'finally', but 'In' is the container signal and 'the end' is a word for the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishes as a verb means comes to an end, the same as stops.

clue.text: Recommend liqueur after losing a point

indicators.note: losing something means dropping it, so one letter is removed from the drink

parts.note: advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur
the letter to drop
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Suggesting a drink once someone has lost a point in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a point' looks like one phrase, but 'a' is the letter dropped and 'point' adds a compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course of action is to argue publicly in favour of it, which is to recommend it.

clue.text: Free newspaper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not ruled or controlled by another
second meaning: The ..., a British national newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a free newspaper handed out at a station; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Independent means self-governing and free of control, and The Independent is a British national newspaper.

clue.text: Fruit is not available after a prohibition begins

indicators.note: begins says the piece it follows stands at the front of the whole word

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
taken as written
N/A is the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: Fruit becomes unobtainable once an import ban starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the abbreviation behind 'a', and 'begins' puts the prohibition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a long curved tropical fruit with yellow skin.

clue.text: Went round Germany by bike?

parts.note: a cycle is a bike
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Touring Germany on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means next to, so the country's letter sits beside the bike; the whole clue also describes a cycle tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cycled went round in a repeating circuit, as seasons or wheels do.

clue.text: In retrospect, see princess as someone to worship

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
Di, Princess Diana, is the usual crossword princess

explanation.surface: Looking back, recognising a princess as an object of devotion, as many did with Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like an ordinary verb, but it stands for the archaic exclamation lo.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person or image greatly admired or adored, an object of worship.

clue.text: Find meaning in this way of speaking a line

parts.note: diction is a person's manner of speaking or enunciation
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Seeking the meaning of how an actor delivers a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase pointing to where meanings are looked up; a railway line abbreviates to RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is the reference book in which you look up what words mean.

clue.text: Could be worth a go

indicators.note: could be suggests the next word might become something else when its letters move

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Saying something might be worth attempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worth a go' is a stock phrase, but it divides into the letters and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throw is a turn at a game of darts or dice, so it is a go.

clue.text: Refrain from raising large amounts

indicators.note: raising lifts things up, and in a down clue reading upwards turns the word backwards

parts.note: pots of money means large amounts

explanation.surface: Holding back from raising lots of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain from' looks like the definition, but 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to hold back from doing something, which is to stop yourself.

clue.text: More wholesome cure by Doctor Reith

parts.note: to heal is to cure

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the name's letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor named Reith offering a more wholesome remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Reith' looks like a person's title and name, but 'Doctor' is a verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthier means better for health, which is what more wholesome means.

clue.text: Profit is something to conceal, we are told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a veil is a thing used to hide the face

explanation.surface: A cynic remarking that profits are things best kept hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means benefit or advantage, as in 'of no avail', close to profit.

clue.text: Difficult to climb the French tower

parts.note: a steep slope is hard to climb
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French tower that is hard to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French tower' suggests the Eiffel Tower, but 'the French' is just the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower topped by a spire.

clue.text: Perverse means to attract backing

parts.note: a way is a means of doing something

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it

explanation.surface: A perverse method of winning support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' looks like a verb defining the answer, but it is a noun meaning method.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward describes someone wilful and hard to control, which is perverse behaviour.
